title: Dream Blunt Rotation: Playtest!
author: enterguild
selftext:
Hey guys, i'm working on an experimental hangout simulator called Dream Blunt Rotation! You pick your dream rotation from a infinite roster, light up, and just talk about whatever. Fully voiced characters riff off each other, argue, yada yada. They get weird over the course of the session - Don't be afraid to join them! You can make new characters or use the existing community ones.

There's no quest. No score. Sit back, relax, and let us know what you honestly think of our little silly experiment! I think the game is best played alone and at night, it's more scratching a social itch (no pun intended) than an actual game. Thank you guys!!!  
  
Link: [itch](https://gothmogged.itch.io/dream-blunt-rotation)

comments.author: jeebiuss
comments.body: Is this three js or unity?

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body: Oh sorry I should have specified, it's Mac and windows (Unity) We run TTS locally so we can't get it working in browser, too heavy

replies.author: jeebiuss
replies.body: Looks really good, how long have you worked on it?

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body: Thank you! We changed ideas a bunch so a few months I think trying to get LLMs to work in games. This was the only concept that I enjoyed the prototype of.

replies.author: jeebiuss
replies.body: Where do you think it helped push the development and where do you think there were friction points in trying to implement LLMs into your workflow

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body: Oh we've been doing this since 2021 I believe, the hard part has been working into a coherent game flow. Something about games and live LLMs natuirally just fights each other, unless you do a gimick game like Suck up or AI2U where it's meant more as a streamer bait toy than a game. You can't fight the LLM I think is the big thing, but we'll see if i'm full of shite lol

comments.author: Turbo-Hugo
comments.body:
Nice idea actually, I dig the strangeness of it!

So, are all conversations AI-generated as you play the game, no scripts?

How did you develop the voices of the characters to resemble their referents?

How did you build it?

I think this is good raw material to be proud about. Well done!

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body:
Thank you!! Yep, it's all live generated and tailored to your own interests as you put in the prompt, so you can talk about whatever is relevant to you, or the characters you hang out with. It really depends on who you choose and how you want to drive it. It just feels like hanging out with friends who you have history with.

You can download and see! The community made characters come from 3d clones of images and voice clones, but you're welcome to test it out yourself. It all works in the game.

Thanks, i'd like for you try it and let me know what you think but I appreciate it nonetheless!!! 😉

replies.author: AirFrierMachine
replies.body: How tf are you paying the cost for the tokens? Someone needs to pay for it, genuinely curious where the money comes from

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body: Self funding it for now, eventually (not anytime soon) we do plan to release on steam and either let ppl use their own API keys or pay through some in app currency thing to cover usage. Making community characters will probably stay free because they scale, we might even reward players who make popular high quality community characters with tokens!

comments.author: Unusual-Cake8234
comments.body: How quickly can you get the voice lines to generate? Is there any overhead for covering the credits? I tried sticking a local llm in my project but it took like 15+ seconds to generate an output.

replies.author: Unusual-Cake8234
replies.body: Very cool idea by the way, viral potential is so high with this

replies.author: enterguild
replies.body: Thank you! We actually use claude for a remote LLM but run TTS locally, yeah local models just aren't fast or good enough for this kind of dialogue unfortunately. We stream it and have had success with both haiku and sonnet (claude) so it's pretty damn fast, you don't really notice it. Give it a try and let me know what you think though!
